bullets.title: THE MORNING FIRE WROTE UP THE ESSAY AND MISSED THE REPRICING — AMODEI'S PACE-THE-FRONTIER POST TOOK THE SECTOR DOWN ON 14 SEPTEMBER, AND MONEY ROTATED OUT OF COMPUTE AND INTO GOVERNANCE
bullets.summary: Archive grep on selloff, sell-off, pledge, Cathie Wood, moratorium: zero hits across the entire archive. The essay is covered — yesterday's fire read darioamodei.com/post/we-must-pace-the-frontier at the primary and logged Altman's and Musk's agreement. The market consequence is not, and it is the larger fact. Monday: Nvidia -3.4%, PHLX semiconductor index -6%, SK Hynix -7.3%, Samsung -5%, SoftBank -10.7% in Tokyo, Micron and SanDisk -6%, memory leading. And the part that matters more than the drawdown: software and cybersecurity shares RALLIED, pulling the major indexes off their lows.
bullets.how: YES — the first price signal this report has ever recorded for the thesis PRAGMA sells. For fourteen days the argument that verification, auditability and governance are the durable layer has been made from vendor behaviour and our own conviction; on Monday a market moved capital out of the capability layer into the control layer inside one session. Not proof the thesis is right, but the first time it has been PRICED rather than argued — a far better citation for a buyer than another changelog. Note also what it says about the instrument: the morning fire read the primary essay correctly and in full, and still missed a sector-wide repricing any market tab would have shown by 09:30 ET.

bullets.title: A CREATIVE-OPS MCP SHIPPED TODAY WITH 96 TOOLS, OAUTH AND NO API KEYS — AND OUR OWN ARCHIVE SHOWS WE FLAGGED THIS EXACT VENDOR 63 DAYS AGO AND NEVER ACTED
bullets.summary: ImagineArt (Vyro AI) launched an MCP server exposing 96 native tools for image, video and music generation callable inside ChatGPT, Claude, Cursor and Grok. No API keys — OAuth against an existing account, billed against existing credits; ChatGPT plugin directory, Claude web by pasting the connector URL. Aggregates Sora, Veo, Kling, Runway and Midjourney behind one connection, plus two guided pipelines: Ad Studio (product-avatar-hook-background to finished video ad) and Fashion Studio. Dateline read at the page: article:published_time 2026-09-15T12:07:50+05:00. Archive grep: ImagineArt and Vyro zero hits, BUT imagine.art hits 2026-07-14, where this report wrote 'Standardize on ONE creative-ops MCP behind graphic-designer.'
bullets.how: YES, and the most actionable item of the day for B9. The vendor is not new; the DISTRIBUTION is — July's raw MCP endpoint is now a keyless OAuth connector installable from a directory, removing the only friction that made the July recommendation feel like a project. Vector's pipeline currently routes through a Higgsfield-class MCP whose credit state has been a recurring blocker; an Ad Studio that assembles a finished video ad from a product and a hook is directly the signage-marketing motion. Reported at trade-press confidence — vendor claims, read at a dated primary page, not a vendor primary. The finding with teeth is not the launch: it is that a recommendation we wrote to ourselves on 14 July has been carried 63 days unexecuted and the ecosystem has now removed its last excuse.

bullets.title: THE MIRROR WAS STALE, SO IT PROVED NOTHING — BUT AN INDEPENDENT SOURCE CONFIRMS 2.1.271, AND THE SEARCH LAYER SERVED ITS MIS-ATTRIBUTED PACKAGE A FOURTH TIME PLUS A FIFTH MIS-DATE
bullets.summary: The morning fire claimed 2.1.271 shipped 14 Sep with omitClaudeMd and per-command allowed_domains. Tested. code.claude.com was NOT reachable — the fetch layer refused it as outside the provenance set, reported rather than papered over. The Releasebot mirror was read end-to-end instead: newest entry 2.1.270 (12 Sep), and omitClaudeMd and allowed_domains appear nowhere — but the page self-reports 'Last updated: Sep 12, 2026', so the mirror is stale and can neither confirm nor refute. An absent string in a snapshot predating the release is not a negative result; it is no result. Independent corroboration found instead: a third-party changelog-tracking repo carries an issue titled '[CHANGELOG v2.1.271] agent frontmatter omitClaudeMd', describing the boolean that lets subagents run without user/project/local CLAUDE.md while managed policy files still load. The morning fire stands. Meanwhile the search layer returned claude plugin eval (2.1.269, 11 Sep), browser-tab icons (2.1.268), the high-CPU fix (2.1.268) and 'Opus 5 default for seat-based Enterprise' (2.1.261, 5 Sep) as a 15 September release — fourth serving in three days. A fifth, new in shape: Claude for Teachers returned as a September announcement. It is 14 July 2026, covered here 15 Jul, 16 Jul and 29 Aug.
bullets.how: YES — and the discipline point is the refusal to convert a stale snapshot into a finding. Calling an absent string in a Sep-12 capture 'evidence against a Sep-14 release' would be the exact error this report catches other people making four times a week. The claim was instead closed at an independent source, and the unreachable primary is recorded as unreachable.

bullets.title: THE ARCHIVE FALSIFIED THIS MORNING'S OWN LEAD — THE LAB DID NOT START SHIPPING VERTICAL SKILL PACKS ON 14 SEPTEMBER, IT STARTED ON 14 JULY, AND WE WROTE THE THESIS DOWN AT THE TIME
bullets.summary: The morning fire read Claude for Financial Advisors as the moment skills-plus-connectors became a public product architecture, and started a clock on that basis. Checking the mis-dated Teachers item against the archive turned up our own entry of 15 July, verbatim: 'the sellable unit is a skills pack + curriculum connections + a data-governance addendum, given away free' and 'the sellable unit is never the model — it's a bounded skill pack plus a written governance posture.' Teachers shipped a library of teaching skills, connections to curricula mapped to standards in all 50 states, and a FERPA-aligned K-12 DPA; it went free to whole districts on 28 Aug (covered 29 Aug).
bullets.how: YES — the correction cuts in our favour on substance and against us on process. Substance: the pattern is two months older than this morning claimed and has produced at least three dated vertical packs (Teachers 14 Jul, districts 28 Aug, Financial Advisors 14 Sep). A trend with three dated instances is far stronger to show a buyer than a single release, and it makes the morning's 'build where headquarters cannot reach' conclusion more urgent, not less. Process: this report had the falsifying evidence in its own files and did not consult it before writing a novelty claim. The 14 Sep method upgrade greps CANDIDATES to kill duplicates; it does not grep the THESIS. Only the second check would have caught this.

bullets.title: STANDING ACTIONS — DAY FIFTEEN, SECOND FIRE. ONE NEW ITEM, AT 63 DAYS, WHICH IS OLDER THAN EVERY ITEM ALREADY ON THE LIST
bullets.summary: NEW: (f) standardize on ONE creative-ops MCP behind graphic-designer — written to ourselves 14 July, carried 63 days, and as of bullet 2 no longer blocked by API-key friction; it enters the list older than (b). CONFIG (unwritten): maxEffortLevel; --system-prompt-snapshot off; CLAUDE_CODE_WORKFLOW_MAX_CONCURRENT_AGENTS still default; per-command allowed_domains; (b) the four Entra MCP controls — ELEVENTH asking, five lines. ARTIFACT: (a) incident log, six rows still in prose, still not queryable; (c) skill-corpus audit — three instruments, zero runs, sixteenth day. READ: RFC 9449, RFC 8707, body of arXiv 2609.00006. CARRIED: OPENROUTER_MODEL=deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash — and this one moved from the vendor side without us: from 04:00 UTC on 14 Sep all deepseek-v4-pro requests route to V4.1-Flash at V4.1-Flash rates until V4.1-Pro launches; also which dsh / ls ~/.dsh; the launchd seam. DEADLINES: Sonar 27 Sep (twelve days), Docusign MCP GA 30 Sep, client-cert 17 Nov, DCR removal after summer 2027. KILLED ON DATELINE, recorded so it is not re-found: Salesforce Agentforce's seven named role-based agents (Casey, Paige, Carter, Hunter, Marshall, Piper, Fin), one per business function, Dreamforce 11 Sep — archive grep zero hits, so new to us but four days stale, and the same named-pack shape as bullets 1 and 4 from a third vendor; Accenture/Google Cloud Gemini Enterprise Business Group killed likewise. EMPTY, REPORTED EMPTY: frontier models — only DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (10 Sep), covered 13 Sep; funding — nothing dated 14-15 Sep; arXiv — nothing newer than 2609.10132 (9 Sep), third consecutive fire empty.
bullets.how: YES — with the observation the fire earns: the oldest open item on this list was written before the report started counting, and the only carried item that moved was moved by the provider at 04:00 UTC yesterday.

praxis_lesson: THE SCAN READS WHAT THE LABS SAY AND MISSES WHAT THE MARKET PAYS — AND YESTERDAY'S LESSON ALREADY SAID SO, ONE LEVEL DOWN. Fire 2 on 14 Sep concluded that a scan whose vendor surface is 'the changelog' will systematically miss pricing, quota, terms and availability, because those are not releases. Today is the same failure with a bigger number attached: the morning fire read Amodei's essay at the primary, correctly, in full — and missed that it took 6% off the semiconductor index, 10.7% off SoftBank and 7.3% off SK Hynix while cybersecurity and software rallied. The essay was the announcement; the rotation was the information. A scan built to answer 'what did they ship' cannot answer 'what did it cost' — and for an ecosystem whose thesis is that the governance layer outlasts the capability layer, Monday was the first day the market voted on that question, and we were reading a blog post. Add the source: watch the tape alongside the changelog. SECOND LESSON, THE HARDER ONE: WE GREP THE ARCHIVE FOR DUPLICATE ITEMS AND NOT FOR CONTRADICTED CLAIMS. The morning fire's lead said the lab 'now' ships vertical skill packs. Our own file of 15 July says the sellable unit is 'a bounded skill pack plus a written governance posture,' about Claude for Teachers, which shipped a teaching-skills library and standards-mapped curriculum connections two months earlier — and we found it only because an aggregator mis-dated Teachers into September and the kill-check dragged it past our eyes. The archive falsified the morning's framing BY ACCIDENT. The 14 Sep upgrade greps candidates to prevent re-reporting; it does nothing to prevent re-DISCOVERING, and a report that rediscovers its own thesis every eight weeks is not compounding. The fix is one line in the method: before writing 'this is new,' grep the archive for the CLAIM, not just the ITEM. THIRD, ON THE ITEM THAT SHOULD EMBARRASS US MOST: today's single most actionable finding is not a launch, it is that standing action (f) is 63 days old — 'standardize on ONE creative-ops MCP' — and the vendor has now removed the API-key friction that made it a project. Sixteen days of standing actions, three instruments pointed at (c) and zero runs, (b) at its eleventh asking, and the oldest open item on the list predates the counting. Meanwhile the one carried item that DID move — deepseek-v4-flash — moved because the provider rerouted it at 04:00 UTC yesterday, which is fire 2's finding stated a third way: everything on this list that changes is being changed by somebody else.
